payload.claim: Neither new test for `witnesses_green_at_base`/`_green_at_base` (`tests/test_criteria.py::test_witnesses_green_at_base_names_the_ones_criteria_would_fail_first`, `..._says_nothing_it_would_not_say_at_a_gate`) nor the new session test (`tests/test_session.py::test_a_witness_green_at_base_is_named_before_the_first_turn`) ever gives a base-side `GateResult` a non-empty `failures` list for the witness under test. Every base fixture in the new tests is 'collected, never failed', so `_green_at_base`'s reliance on `_green`'s `witness not in failed` half is exercised by none of them. Changing the return to `return not criterion.preserves and criterion.witness in before[0]` (checking only `collected`, ignoring `failed`) keeps every new and existing test green, but makes a witness that actually failed at `base_sha` — the ordinary shape of a bug-fix criterion whose regression test already existed and was red before the fix — get wrongly named in `green_at_base` and wrongly fail `criteria` with `witness-green-at-base`, exactly the false-positive this feature must not produce on the class of task it is meant to help most.
